output.brief: The wrong dates are not an operator problem. Printer records show every Veltranol job since 4 Oct 22:10 received a 36-month shelf life from PackBridge, with no operator overrides. Before that, all 30 jobs were correct. This includes jobs after the firmware change and jobs run by agency operators. Two bad jobs ran on Line 1 day shift with permanent staff. On 3 Oct, Regulatory Affairs entered a 36-month value in the ERP, valid only from 1 Mar 2027, for lots made from that date. The 24-month value is still the one in effect. PackBridge nonetheless sent 36 months. That contradicts the vendor's statement that it only uses the value in effect, so the vendor's claim needs testing. I'm fairly confident (about 85%) in this. I don't yet know why PackBridge picked up the future-dated value. Don't discipline or remove the agency operators, and don't switch off the camera check. The camera only checks print against job data, so it can't catch this. Next steps: reset the Veltranol shelf-life record so only the current value can be read. Hold every Veltranol lot packed since 4 Oct, including the two on Line 1 sitting in the warehouse. Add a second-person check of printed expiry against the batch record at each setup. Inspect the products with future-dated edits, HX-15-30 and MR-05-14. Press Corvane to explain how it handles future-dated values. Hold off on a 12-month site-wide review and on over-labelling until those checks show a wider problem.
